A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GCN-DevLSTM study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and supplementary Sections 7.1–7.6 support reliable comparison, including material reorganized between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition accuracies on NTU60, NTU120 and Chalearn2013, together with ablations, sensitivity studies and frame-removal robustness results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds residual-path ablation results and robustness measurements for inserted frames and missing joints.

M1.justification: The architecture, hop-based graph convolution, sliding-window development branches, starting-point concatenation, LSTM, CNN/pooling branches, loss and fusion streams are retained. G-Dev Sequence and Hops-CTRGC formalize or rename operations already described in v1.

E1.justification: The three recognition datasets and tasks remain unchanged. v2 extends NTU60 X-sub evaluation beyond missing frames to inserted frames and missing-joint scenarios, adding distinct input conditions within retained dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their comparator sets; the trailing marker on ST-PSM+L-PSM in v1 is a footnote, not a different method. Added robustness scenarios use the existing CTRGCN and GCN-LSTM comparators.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark splits, NTU preprocessing, batch size and training schedule are retained. Added protocols insert 6–38 interpolated frames and randomly remove joints per frame, testing zero filling and temporal interpolation separately.

E4.justification: Robustness analysis expands substantially from frame removal to frame insertion and joint occlusion under two filling strategies (Figure 3 and Section 7.6). Table 4 also adds a residual-path ablation. Existing backbone, graph-hop and Lie-group sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 Section 7.4 specifies seed 1 for the Lie-group/hidden-size sweep and warns that results may vary across seeds and tasks. v2 removes this disclosure and caveat without adding repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores and previously reported analyses retain their values. Additions include residual-removal accuracies of 89.9/95.2 in Table 4 and new perturbation results. For example, Table 8 reports losses of 5.41, 14.92 and 10.88 percentage points after inserting 38 frames for GCN-DevLSTM, CTRGCN and GCN-LSTM, respectively.

T1.justification: v2 adds synchronized-timestamp assumptions and an invariance-based imputation assertion in Section 3.3. Section 7.1 introduces an endpoint-indicator product that requires both endpoints to match, conflicting with the retained shared-joint criterion. The core path-development equations and derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows its blanket claim of significantly outperforming current best methods to consistently improving strong GCN baselines and achieving state-of-the-art results. The main contributions concerning graph development, temporal modeling, accuracy and robustness remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies dependence on external GCNs for spatial information and proposes neighboring-node aggregation as future work. It adds explanations of streaming efficiency and missing-joint filling tradeoffs, but removes v1's qualification that the Chalearn comparison involves unequal data augmentation.

D1.justification: v2 specifies timestamp alignment and the new robustness tests' interpolation and zero-filling behavior. Hardware, training hyperparameters and the project code URL remain. v1's disclosure that the Cheng et al. baseline code was unavailable is removed; this does not establish changed code availability.

R1.justification: Several background citations change, including additions of Levin et al. (2013) and Zhou et al. (2022), and removals of Chen (1958) and Lou et al. (2023). The synthetic-generation discussion now contains an unresolved [?] citation. The central positioning as an extension of path development remains.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the introduction, related work and method explanation. Sliding-window material moves from Section 4.2 to 3.3, graph-convolution equations move to Section 7.5, and dual-graph interpretation moves into the supplement. The conclusion gains limitations and future-work discussion.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn and reorganized, Figure 3 expands to three panels, and Table 1 adopts stream-checkbox columns. The unchanged hidden-size results move from Figure 6 to Table 6. Robustness tables are expanded or added, while Table 3 loses its column headings.

improvement.justification: The added joint-occlusion and frame-insertion tests substantiate robustness beyond v1's frame-removal evidence. The residual ablation and explicit spatial-dependence limitation also improve assessment of the design. These gains provide a modest net improvement, tempered by lost augmentation and seed disclosures, an unresolved citation and the inconsistent new dual-graph formula.
